intro.text: Humanities-01, this is Mission Control. A big dust storm is coming. It will block about {blocked}% of your sunlight for a few days.
Copy that, Control. On a clear day our panels make {power} power units.
Our extra solar panels will help, but the dust will still cover them.
We only have the basic panels, so this storm is going to hurt.
Good news. Your battery pack can store spare power for the storm.
You packed no extra battery, so we must be careful with every unit of power.
Decide what gets power first. Every choice has a cost.

protect-crew.text: Shield and life support first. The crops will go without light for a while.
Understood. We will watch your food supply closely.

protect-crops.text: Greenhouse first. The food keeps growing, but the shield will be weak.
Then radiation will slowly build up. Keep an eye on it.

keep-science.text: Science first! The instruments keep working, but we will feel it later.
A brave choice. Other systems will have to wait.

intro.text: Humanities-01, our sensors saw a huge solar flare. Fast charged particles will reach you tomorrow.
On the real Mars, such particles can arrive within tens of minutes. In this game, you get one day to prepare.
Copy that. How much will our walls stop?
Your walls only have basic shielding, about {shield}%. Sheltering will matter a lot.
Your extra shield wall helps. Your walls stop about {shield}%.
Understood. What should the crew do?

full-shelter.text: Everyone into the shelter! Research will wait, but we stay safe.
Good. Thick walls stop more of the particles.

partial-shelter.text: We will shelter for part of the day and work in between.
A balance. Some radiation will still get through.

keep-working.text: We keep working. The shield wall has to do the job.
Your shield wall will help a lot.
With only basic shielding, this is risky. Watch the radiation meter.
